title: Quick Garlic Pasta
description: Super fast and delicious pasta recipe.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pasta until al dente.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté minced garlic until fragrant.

title: One-Pan Creamy Garlic Spinach Pasta
description: A rich, comforting pasta that comes together in under 25 minutes using just one skillet. Ideal for busy exam nights with minimal cleanup.
ingredients: 1/2 cup heavy cream (or milk with 1 tsp cornstarch)
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil salted water in a pot and cook pasta until al dente. Reserve 1/4 cup of starchy pasta water before draining.
Heat olive oil or butter in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and red chili flakes, sauteing for 60 seconds until fragrant without browning.
Lower the heat and pour in the heavy cream and reserved pasta cooking water. Simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Toss in the freshly washed baby spinach and stir until gently wilted.
Fold in the cooked pasta and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until a silky, creamy sauce coats every noodle.
Season with salt and fresh cracked pepper. Serve hot with an extra sprinkle of Parmesan.
notes: Student tip: If you don't have heavy cream in your mini-fridge, whisk 1/2 cup of whole milk with a tablespoon of cream cheese or cornstarch.

reviews.comment: Made this during mid-sem prep week. Took literally 20 minutes and barely dirtied dishes. 10/10!
Added some sliced sautéed mushrooms to it. The garlic sauce is spot-on.

title: Homestyle Masala Egg Curry
description: Flavorful, fragrant hard-boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy. Reminds you of home cooking when living away in a college dorm.
ingredients: 2 ripe tomatoes, pureed or finely diced
instructions: Prick the peeled boiled eggs lightly with a fork. Rub with a pinch of turmeric and salt.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pan and shallow fry the eggs for 2-3 minutes until a light golden skin forms. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining oil. Add chopped onions and sauté over medium heat until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and slit green chili. Sauté for 1 minute until raw smell dissipates.
Pour in tomato puree along with turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until oil starts separating from the masala.
Pour in 3/4 cup of warm water, bring the gravy to a gentle simmer, and gently lower the fried eggs into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes so the eggs absorb all the flavors.
Finish with garam masala and freshly chopped coriander. Enjoy warm with steamed rice or rotis.
notes: Student tip: An electric kettle works great for boiling eggs if you're in a hostel room!

reviews.comment: Genuine comfort food! The gravy consistency is perfect with plain basmati rice.

title: Crispy Tofu & Edamame Teriyaki Bowl
description: Golden pan-crisped tofu cubes tossed in a quick 4-ingredient homemade teriyaki glaze, served over fluffy rice with steamed edamame.
ingredients: 250g firm tofu, pressed and cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tablespoons sesame oil or neutral cooking oil
2 cups cooked jasmine or brown rice
Toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions for garnish
instructions: Press the tofu with paper towels to remove excess moisture. Toss cubes in cornstarch until lightly and evenly coated.
Heat sesame oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes in a single layer and pan-fry for 7-8 minutes, turning occasionally until all sides are crunchy and golden.
In a small cup, whisk together soy sauce, honey, grated garlic, and ginger with 2 tablespoons of water.
Pour the glaze directly over the hot crispy tofu in the pan. Simmer for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens into a shiny coating.
Steam or boil the edamame for 3 minutes with a pinch of salt.
Assemble bowls: scoop cooked rice at the base, arrange teriyaki tofu and bright green edamame on top.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onion.
notes: Cost saver: Buy blocks of tofu from local grocery stores; it's one of the cheapest high-protein staples for college budgets.

title: Warm Spiced Chickpea Shakshuka
description: Poached eggs nestled in a hearty, smoky cumin-and-paprika spiced tomato sauce with chickpeas. Perfect for a cozy weekend brunch.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked or canned chickpeas, rinsed
Crumbled feta cheese and chopped parsley to finish
Crusty bread or toasted pita for dipping
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion and red bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper. Stir continuously for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the canned tomatoes and chickpeas. Season with salt and black pepper. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens nicely.
Use the back of a spoon to create 3 shallow wells in the bubbling tomato sauce.
Carefully crack an egg into each well. Cover the skillet with a lid and cook on medium-low for 5 to 7 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks remain soft.
Remove from heat, crumble fresh feta cheese on top, and scatter chopped parsley.
Serve right out of the skillet with thick slices of warm crusty bread.
notes: Great for sharing: Put the whole skillet in the middle of the table with toast and dig in with your roommates.

reviews.comment: The chickpeas make this so filling! We had it for Sunday brunch with toasted sourdough.

title: Overnight Oats with Chia, Banana & Berries
description: Zero morning cooking required. Mix oats, chia seeds, and milk the night before in a mason jar for a grab-and-go morning breakfast before early lectures.
ingredients: Handful of blueberries or chopped strawberries
1 tablespoon peanut butter or crushed walnuts
instructions: In a clean jar or small airtight container, combine rolled oats, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Pour in milk and sweetener (honey or maple syrup). Stir thoroughly with a spoon so no dry pockets remain.
Seal the container and place it in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight.
In the morning, give it a quick stir. If it is too thick, splash in a tablespoon of milk.
Top with sliced banana, fresh berries, and a dollop of peanut butter right before eating.
notes: Prep-ahead hero: Make 3 or 4 jars on Sunday night and you're set for breakfast throughout the week.

title: Classic Vegetable Pulao with Mint & Raita
description: Fragrant basmati rice gently cooked with whole spices, green peas, carrots, and potatoes. A balanced, budget-friendly one-pot meal.
ingredients: 1.5 cups long grain Basmati rice, washed and soaked for 20 mins
1/2 cup fresh or frozen green peas
1 bay leaf, 2 green cardamoms, 1 inch cinnamon stick, 3 cloves
instructions: Rinse basmati rice until the water runs clear and let it soak in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat ghee or oil in a deep pot. Add the whole spices: cumin seeds, bay leaf, cardamoms, cinnamon, and cloves. Let them crackle for 30 seconds.
Add sliced onions and green chilies. Sauté until the onions turn translucent and light golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add diced carrots, potatoes, and green peas. Sauté the vegetables for 2-3 minutes.
Add the drained basmati rice, chopped mint, and coriander. Gently mix for 1 minute without breaking the long rice grains.
Pour in 3 cups of water and add salt. Bring to a rolling boil.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover with a tight lid, and cook undisturbed for 12-14 minutes.
Turn off heat and let it rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork and serve with cucumber raita.
notes: Leftover hack: Tastes even better the next day for campus lunch. Pack in a thermal lunch box.

title: Fudgy 5-Minute Banana Mug Cake
description: Craving something sweet while studying late? This egg-free, warm chocolate-banana mug cake cooks in 90 seconds in a microwave.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour (maida or whole wheat flour)
1.5 tablespoons brown sugar or regular sugar
1 tablespoon melted butter or vegetable oil
instructions: In a standard microwave-safe ceramic mug, thoroughly mash the ripe banana with a fork until smooth.
Add milk and melted butter to the mug. Stir to combine.
Add flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking powder, and pinch of salt. Mix with a small fork until a smooth batter forms.
Drop chocolate chips into the center of the batter if desired (they will sink and create a melted molten center).
Microwave on high power for 70 to 90 seconds. The top should look cooked through and springy.
Allow to cool for 2 minutes before eating directly from the mug.
notes: Hostel favorite: All you need is a fork and a coffee mug. No oven, no beater, no mess.

reviews.comment: Literal lifesaver at 1 AM while writing lab reports. Added peanut butter instead of choc chips!

title: Sheet Pan Lemon Herb Roasted Veggies & Paneer
description: Toss colorful seasonal vegetables and paneer cubes with lemon juice, oregano, and olive oil, then bake until tender and charred at the edges.
ingredients: 1 zucchini or yellow squash, sliced into half-moons
1 red bell pepper, cut into bite-sized chunks
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat your oven or toaster oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place paneer cubes, zucchini, bell pepper, onion wedges, and cherry tomatoes directly onto the baking tray.
In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, lemon juice, dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Drizzle the dressing over the vegetables and paneer. Use your hands to toss gently until everything is evenly coated.
Spread the ingredients into a single flat layer so they roast rather than steam.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the veggies are tender and the edges of the paneer are slightly golden and caramelized.
Squeeze extra lemon juice over top and serve warm with couscous, rice, or flatbread.
notes: Meal prep tip: Roasting a double batch on Sunday gives you quick lunches for three days.
